text:
nina: Heads up — Acme POC failing on private endpoint in ap-southeast-1. Clients see TLS handshake failures and our SDK times out. Can network/security triage?

carl: What exact errors? Any gateway logs?

nina: Client: `tls: handshake failure` then `context deadline exceeded` after ~9s. Gateway log snippets attached by support: 
```
2026-03-05T10:11:02Z outbound: dial tcp 10.10.22.33:80: i/o timeout
2026-03-05T10:11:02Z tls: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
2026-03-05T10:11:02Z ocsp: fetch failed: lookup ocsp.digica.net on 172.16.0.2:53: no such host
```

devon: Sounds like split-horizon DNS where `ocsp.digica.net` resolves to an RFC1918 address inside their VPC that our runtime can't reach, or their resolver blocks egress to that subnet.

andy: Actionable checklist to ask customer to run from the connector host/container: 
1) `dig +short ocsp.digica.net @<their-resolver>`
2) `getent hosts ocsp.digica.net`
3) `openssl s_client -connect ocsp.digica.net:80 -status -servername ocsp.digica.net`
4) `tcpdump -s0 -w /tmp/ocsp.pcap tcp and host ocsp.digica.net`
Please run as root so the pcap contains the handshake.

nina: Procurement wants cost options if they need us to run inside their VPC or provide an egress proxy. @acct-bot can you confirm POC pricing for a 30-day private deployment trial + managed egress?

acct-bot: Quote estimate: Private trial — 14 days free for POC. Extended 30-day private trial + managed egress (temporary) estimated uplift: ~25% over base Dedicated list. Professional services for proxy setup billed hourly. Exact quote requires account team approval.

carl: Short-term mitigations we can propose to Acme: 1) they add firewall rule to allow outbound to the CA's published OCSP IPs (least change), 2) they run a customer-managed OCSP mirror reachable from our connector, 3) we spin up a short-term Private deployment in their VPC (fastest from network perspective), 4) temporarily disable OCSP validation on the client for the POC (last-resort; security signoff required).

devon: Also check SNI rewriting by their TLS inspection appliances. If SNI gets stripped/rewritten the CA responder may refuse and cause handshake failures. If `openssl s_client -servername` succeeds but runtime fails, capture the pcap and we can analyze.

nina: I'll send a minimal triage note to them with the dig/openssl/tcpdump checklist and ask whether their resolver returns RFC1918 addresses for public OCSP hosts or CNAMEs to internal hosts.

acct-bot: Incident logged: POC-20260305-APSE-OCSP  assigned to eng-netops for investigation.

andy: One practical thing: if they cannot change egress rules and they want to proceed without Private deployment, we can offer to host a short-lived proxy in our cloud that the connector uses via an authenticated tunnel. That requires IPSec/VPN or a peering arrangement and PS engagement.

carl: Good. Ask them for the dig output first; that will tell us whether we need to push for network changes vs a proxy.

nina: Sending checklist now. Will update when we get outputs. :white_check_mark:
